reason:
The PROBLEM is real and I reproduced it to the decimal; the FIX as written would ship a visible regression into a protected state, so it is refuted with the corrected fix below. Verified by driving lately.html in chromium at 1440/768/390 across all seven states: the only reset in the file is `* { box-sizing: border-box }` (line 109) plus `body { margin: 0 }` (line 114) and `.page { margin: 0 auto }` (line 167) — there is no p/h reset anywhere. Computed margins in state=full match the seat exactly: .t-label P 11/11, .t-small P 13/13, .t-head 20/20, .t-sect 21.58/21.58 on the three

s (and 17.42 on the one

, an asymmetry the seat did not mention that makes band one's heading sit 4px tighter than bands two to four). Rendered gaps match: .limit eyebrow-to-heading 39px and heading-to-explanation 41px against an authored 8px, tile height 216.13px; .ghost-say 37px against an authored 4px (the seat says --gap-tight here; it is actually --gap-hair); .stack 23px against 8px. One number is stated inconsistently: at 390 the .reading wrapped-row gap is 34px, not 49px — 48.85px is the row-to-row pitch, not the gap the other four numbers are. The point stands either way (12px appears nowhere), and the seat is right that audit.mjs cannot see any of it: its spacing rule (scripts/audit.mjs:626) regexes the SOURCE for raw px >4 inside margin/padding/gap, so a UA margin is invisible to it, and `margin: 0` will not trip it. Crops of .limits before and after the reset confirm the consequence claim rather than the taste of it — at 39px the 'NOT YET' eyebrow floats free of its heading and the tile reads as three fragments; at 12px it reads as one object. Severity `defect` is correctly classed: nothing untrue is asserted and the product still works, but the declared ladder is overridden everywhere and the gap scales with font size, contradicting the file's own 'Leading belongs to a role, not to a size'. Why the fix is refused: it names four containers and misses the fifth and largest. `.center` also holds

and

children and carries the ENTIRE composition of the quiet, empty and error states — two of them the protected honest-degradation states. Applying the reset with only the four named retunes collapses .center from gaps [53, 27, 23] to a flat [12, 12, 12]: the 'Try again' button crowds the copy and the LAST GOOD READING timestamp crowds the button. That is a state left worse than it is today, so as written the fix is not an improvement at the declared bar. It also misses .band-head, where the section heading's standoff from its band content drops from ~38px to the bare 16px padding-bottom in all four bands, and .top-row (65px to 30px).
sharpenedFix: Keep the reset — `h1, h2, h3, p { margin: 0; }` immediately after `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` — and verify it is sufficient: I confirmed no <ul>, <ol>, <li>, <dl>, <blockquote>, <figure>, <pre>, <table> or <h4>-<h6> renders in any of the seven states, so those four selectors cover every UA-margined element on the surface today. Then retune SIX containers, not four, all on ladder tokens: (1) `.limit` --gap-tight to --gap-snug (12px, verified by crop); (2) `.ghost-say` --gap-hair to --gap-snug — note its current rung is --gap-hair, not --gap-tight as the finding states; (3) `.stack` --gap-tight to --gap-line (16px); (4) `.reading` split the shorthand to `gap: var(--gap-line) var(--gap-snug)` so the inline rhythm stays 12px but the wrapped row at 390 gets 16px instead of dropping from 34px to 12px directly under a 24px padding-top; (5) NEW — `.center` --gap-snug to --gap-line, plus `.center .btn { margin-top: var(--gap-tight); }` so the action keeps a 24px standoff from the copy it acts on, then re-shoot quiet, empty and error before accepting; (6) NEW — `.band-head` padding-bottom --gap-line to --gap-room, so a 26px section head does not sit 16px off its content in all four bands. Also drop the <h1>/<h2> asymmetry note into the commit: with UA margins gone, band one's heading finally sits at the same standoff as bands two to four.
breaks: Every height in the lab goes stale. Measured scrollHeight after the reset: full 1899 to 1540, partial 2024 to 1634, quiet 2074 to 1645, first-run 1902 to 1540, loading 1360 to 1132, phone full 3188 to 2532; empty and error still fit the viewport. All ten frames in shots/ must be re-shot, and report.html / console.html re-derived from them. Re-measure specifically: (a) `.hero-fig` drops 236 to 191 while `.chart` is fixed — the .hero grid is `align-items: stretch` so they stayed matched in my run, but confirm the hero card is now driven by the chart column and not by the shrunken text column at 1280 and 768; (b) interaction-check.mjs lines 371-372, `the skeleton hero is the real hero's height` and `the skeleton card is the real card's height`, are the only assertions in either gate with a pixel tolerance (8px) — the skeleton is literally the same DOM so it should track, but this is the one that can flip; (c) line 407, `the refusals carry the same rank as the findings`, compares two .t-sect bounding heights, which margins do not enter, so it is safe but should be re-run; (d) `.note` 109 to 79 and `.card.ages` 239 to 199 shift the .dot positions the strip/tip assertions drive against — they use scrollIntoViewIfNeeded so they should hold, but re-run the touch pass at 390. audit.mjs is unaffected by the reset itself (`margin: 0` carries no raw px), but every retune must use a --gap-* token or it will trip the source spacing rule.
